facts.statement: Anguanax is an extinct genus of basal pliosaurid.
facts.quote: taxon: Anguanax

facts.statement: Anguanax lived during the Late Jurassic period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic,

facts.statement: Anguanax is known solely from the holotype specimen MPPL 18797, which is housed at the Museo Paleontologico e della Preistoria 'P. Leonardi' in Ferrara.
facts.quote: Anguanax is known solely from the holotype MPPL 18797, currently housed at the Museo Paleontologico e della Preistoria 'P. Leonardi' in Ferrara.

facts.statement: The remains were collected during the 1980s from the Kaberlaba quarry in the Asiago Municipality of the Vicenza Province in northern Italy.
facts.quote: It was collected during the 1980s from a nodular and cherty limestone interval at the Kaberlaba quarry in the Asiago Municipality of the Vicenza Province of northern Italy.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the middle Oxfordian stage of the early Late Jurassic, approximately 160 million years ago.
facts.quote: This interval belongs to Lithozone 5 of the Middle Unit of the Rosso Ammonitico Veronese Formation which dates to the middle Oxfordian stage of the early Late Jurassic, about 160 million years ago.

facts.statement: Although discovered in the 1980s, the specimen was not thoroughly described until 2014 by Andrea Cau and Federico Fanti.
facts.quote: Despite its discovery during the 1980s, MPPL 18797 was only first thoroughly described by Andrea Cau and Federico Fanti in 2014, and was found to represent the first articulated skeleton of an Italian plesiosaurian.

facts.statement: The genus was named in 2015 by Cau and Fanti, with the type species designated as Anguanax zignoi.
facts.quote: The specimen was named in 2015 by Cau and Fanti following the preparation of additional bones, with the type species being Anguanax zignoi.

facts.statement: Anguanax was a medium-sized carnivorous basal pliosaurid with an estimated body length of 3 to 4 meters.
facts.quote: Anguanax is a medium-sized carnivorous basal pliosaurid, at an estimated body length of about 3 - 4 m.

facts.statement: Anguanax has two unique traits: a palpebral projection at the midheight of the eye socket margin and a distinct trapezoidal posteroventral coracoid process.
facts.quote: Anguanax possesses two unique traits among other plesiosaurians including a projection on the palpebral placed at midheight of the front-facing margin of the eye socket; and a posteroventral process of coracoid developed as a distinct trapezoid that does not reach the glenoid level from the side, and with a straight margin directed back and to the side from its back facing position.

facts.statement: Anguanax is distinguished by a combination of rare traits including narrow neural spines, a back-directed retroarticular projection, a hill on the coronoid depression, and specific rib facet placements.
facts.quote: Additionally, other traits are relatively rare in pliosaurids and thus their combination in Anguanax distinguishes it from other pliosaurids. These include narrow axial neural spines, a back-directed retroarticular projection on the vertebrae, a hill on the coronoid depression, a stepped posteroventral corner of the back margin of the eye socket, rib facets that are placed dorsally on caudal vertebrae but does not extended to the neural arches, and front cervical centra that bear a low and broad midline ridge on their bottom surface.

facts.statement: Anguanax belongs to the family Pliosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Pliosauridae

facts.statement: The genus Anguanax was described by Cau and Fanti in 2015.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Cau & Fanti, 2015

facts.statement: Anguanax is an extinct basal pliosaurid genus found in Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) rocks of the Rosso Ammonitico Veronese Formation in northern Italy.
facts.quote: Anguanax es un género extinto de pliosáurido basal cuyos restos proceden de rocas del Jurásico Superior (época del Oxfordiense) de la Formación Rosso Ammonitico Veronese en el norte de Italia.

facts.statement: Originally described as exclusively plesiosaurian by Zigno, the remains were later found to include crocodylomorph elements, though neither group could be identified to the family level.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron descritos originalmente como pertenecientes exclusivamente a plesiosaurios por Zigno, si bien posteriormente se determinó que incluían elementos de crocodilomorfos también, aunque ninguno de estos pudo ser identificado hasta el nivel de familia taxonómica.

facts.statement: The species name honors Zigno for discovering the first plesiosaurian remains from the Rosso Ammonitico Veronese Formation.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie es en homenaje de Zigno por haber descubierto los primeros restos de plesiosaurios de la Formación Rosso Ammonitico Veronese.

facts.statement: Anguanax was a medium-sized basal pliosaurid predator with an estimated body length of 3 to 4 meters based on the holotype.
facts.quote: Anguanax era un pliosáurido basal depredador de tamaño mediano, con una longitud corporal estimada en unos 3–4 metros basándose en el holotipo.

facts.statement: Anguanax had body proportions generally similar to other primitive pliosaurids, such as the well-preserved Peloneustes.
facts.quote: Sus proporciones corporales se parecen en general a las de otros pliosáuridos primitivos, por ejemplo el bien preservado Peloneustes.

facts.statement: Anguanax likely fed on small or soft-bodied prey in the upper pelagic zone, indicated by its moderately expanded lateral-facing eye orbits, slender elongated jaw, and small curved teeth with finely serrated edges.
facts.quote: Anguanax se alimentaba de presas pequeñas o de cuerpo blando en la zona pelágica superior de su ambiente, como lo sugieren las órbitas oculares moderadamente expandidas y orientadas hacia los lados, la mandíbula grácil y relativamente alargada, y los pequeños y delgados dientes curvos dotados con un borde finamente aserrado.

facts.statement: Anguanax possesses two unique traits compared to other plesiosaurs: a palpebral bone projection located midway along the front margin of the eye orbit, and a posterior-ventral coracoid process shaped like a trapezoid that does not reach the level of the glenoid cavity from its side.
facts.quote: Anguanax posee dos rasgos únicos con respecto a los demás plesiosaurios incluyendo una proyección del hueso palpebral situada a mitad de la zona media del margen frontal de la órbita ocular; y un proceso posterior-ventral del coracoides en forma de trapezoide que no alcanza al nivel de la cavidad glenoidea desde su costado, y con un margen recto dirigido hacia atrás y hacia un lado desde su posición vuelta hacia atrás.

facts.statement: Anguanax is distinguished by a combination of rare pliosaurid traits, including narrow neural spines on the axis, a posteriorly directed retroarticular process on vertebrae, a peak in the coronoid depression, a posterovergent corner on the rear margin of the eye orbit, rib articular surfaces located dorsally on caudal vertebrae but not extending to neural arches, and low broad crests on the mid-lower surface of cervical vertebral centers.
facts.quote: Adicionalmente, posee otros rasgos que son relativamente raros en los pliosáuridos y cuya combinación permite distinguir a Anguanax de los demás pliosáuridos. Estos incluyen las estrechas espinas neurales en el axis, una proyección retroarticular dirigida hacia atrás en las vértebras, una cima en la depresión del coronoides, una esquina descendente posteroventral en el margen posterior de la órbita ocular, superficies articulares de las costillas que se sitúan dorsalmente en las vértebras caudales pero no se extienden hasta los arcos neurales, y los centros frontales de las vértebras cervicales poseen una cresta baja y ancha en el medio de su superficie inferior.

facts.statement: Anguanax lived during the Callovian to Oxfordian stages, approximately 165.3 to 159 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Callovian to Oxfordian (165.3 to 159 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Anguanax was named by Cau and Fanti in 2016.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Anguanax (genus), Cau and Fanti 2016
